intro: To record a slide show in PowerPoint on Mac, open the deck in the desktop app and choose Slide Show > Record Slide Show. Pick Presenter view or Teleprompter, press Record, and PowerPoint saves your narration and slide timings inside the file.
tldr: Use the desktop app. PowerPoint for the web cannot record slide shows, so open PowerPoint for Mac instead.
Start with Slide Show > Record Slide Show, or the Record button in the top-right corner, depending on your build.
Let each transition finish before you speak. Narration does not record during slide transitions.
To share a video, choose File > Export, pick MP4 with HEVC, and keep Use Recorded Timings and Narrations checked.

blocks.text: What you need before you record

You need the desktop app. PowerPoint for the web cannot record slide shows. Microsoft's feature comparison marks recording as supported on PowerPoint for Mac and PowerPoint for PC, and as not supported on the web, Android, iOS and mobile. Open PowerPoint from Applications or the Dock, then open the deck you want to narrate.

Next, check your build number. Video export with narration needs Microsoft 365 for Mac, and Microsoft says narration is included in video exports from build 16.19. A Microsoft Q&A moderator named 16.60 for narrated recording, so update if you are older than that. Open PowerPoint > About PowerPoint to read the number.

items: A microphone. The built-in one works, and an external microphone usually sounds cleaner.
A camera, only if you want presenter video in the recording.
Camera and microphone access for PowerPoint in System Settings.
A quiet room, and a few bullet points or a script for each slide.

blocks.title: Check the build first
blocks.text: A quick look at About PowerPoint saves confusion later. If the Record option is missing, update through Help > Check for Updates, then look again.
Where the Record command lives on Mac

This is the part that trips people up. Microsoft's own pages do not describe the same menu. The training page says to click Record in the top-right corner, or to choose Record > From Beginning or Record > From Current Slide. The Tech Community post and a Microsoft Q&A moderator describe Slide Show > Record Slide Show instead.

rows: Record button top-right, or Record > From Beginning / From Current Slide
Slide Show > Record Slide Show, with Clear recording to the left of Record
Insiders on Mac Fast 16.43 or later
Slide Show tab > Record Slide Show, then Presenter View
blocks.caption: Three Microsoft sources describe the same feature with different menu paths.

blocks.text: Here is how to handle it. Look at the menu bar first. If you see a Slide Show tab with Record Slide Show, use that. If the top-right corner of the window shows a Record button, use that. The steps in this guide cover both, and your screen decides which one you use.
Set your microphone, camera and view

Set your devices before you press Record. The recording toolbar has an audio dropdown and a video dropdown. Pick your microphone from the audio list. Pick your camera from the video list. If you turn the video button off, PowerPoint records audio only, which works fine for a voice-over on slides.

Choose Presenter view if you want your notes and the next slide visible while you talk. Choose Teleprompter if you read from a script. Camera options also include a blur background, which helps when your room has clutter behind you.

blocks.title: Microphone silent?
blocks.text: Turn PowerPoint's microphone access off and on in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone, then quit and reopen the app. Check System Settings > Sound > Input too. One Microsoft Q&A thread says reinstalling did not help, so test a short recording before a big session.
Record, pause and fix a slide

Press Record and wait a moment before you speak. Each slide records as you move through the deck. Use the arrow keys or a click to advance. Pause with the pause button when you need a break, then resume from the same spot.

Transitions cause most of the clipped narration people report. Microsoft says narration does not record during slide transitions. Let the animation finish, then speak. The pause feels slow while you record, but it saves you from cutting out half-sentences later.

If a slide goes wrong, don't record the whole deck again. Select the trash-can button to the left of the Record button, then record that slide again. The Record tab also offers Clear Recording and Reset to Cameo, for the current slide or for all slides.
Keyboard shortcuts while recording on Mac

Keep your hands on the keyboard. Microsoft lists a few Mac shortcuts for recording. Esc exits the recording. Command+. ends the slide show. Command+P switches the pointer to a pen, and Command+A switches it back to the arrow. Control+H hides the arrow when the mouse moves.

The Windows keys R, S and Alt+S do not apply on a Mac, even though some guides still show them. Microsoft's list is short and does not show an Option or Shift shortcut for recording, so do not count on one.
Pen, laser and ink in the recording

Ink and pointer movement can go into the recording too. Right-click during the show, choose Pointer Options, then Pen, and your ink is captured. Laser Pointer records cursor movement. Microsoft's Tech Community post describes both. Use them sparingly, since a moving pointer can pull viewers away from your words.
Review, re-record and end the recording

When you finish, press Esc to exit the recording. Then use Preview Play to watch it back before you export. Watch for clipped words, a missing camera, and slides that started too early. Re-record only the slides that need it.

Recordings are embedded in the slides and play during Slide Show. A separate video file comes only from export. That means you can fix one slide and record it again later without rebuilding the whole show.
Export the recording as an MP4 video

Most people want a file they can send. Choose File > Export. In the File Format menu, pick the MP4 option that uses HEVC. Microsoft offers four sizes: Ultra HD 4K, Full HD 1080p, HD 720p and Standard 480p. Pick the one that matches where the video will play.

rows: Large screens and slides with fine detail
Most video platforms and laptop screens
blocks.caption: The four resolutions in Microsoft's Mac video export.

blocks.text: Keep Use Recorded Timings and Narrations checked. If you clear it, you set how long each slide shows, and the recorded narration is ignored. Microsoft also warns that other embedded media may not play in the export. Open the exported file and test it before you send it anywhere.
Some builds also list Record > Export to video, which Microsoft's training page mentions. Both routes produce an MP4 file. Use whichever menu your build shows.
Fixing microphone, version and playback problems

Most problems come down to three things: an old build, a blocked microphone, or a transition that cut your narration. Start with the build. Then check the microphone permission. Then check the slide transitions. The Microsoft Q&A threads on this topic point at the same three areas.
Why narrated recordings still matter

People do watch recorded lessons. A 2019 University of Leeds study of 1,734 students found that the share who watched at least one lecture video rose from 50.4% to 81.4% over the study period. Students watched about 10 recordings each on average. The study covered lecture capture in general, not narrated PowerPoint, so treat it as context rather than a benchmark.

The same study has a downside. 53.6% of instructors agreed that lecture capture encouraged poor attendance, and 50.8% of lecturers said it hindered their spontaneity. Keep your narration natural, and keep slides short enough that a live session still feels worth attending.
Mistakes people make when recording slides

items: Trying to record in PowerPoint for the web, which cannot record slide shows.
Skipping the build check, then hunting for a Record option that is not there.
Talking over transitions, so the first words of each slide get lost.
Clearing Use Recorded Timings and Narrations during export, then wondering why the voice vanished.
Recording the whole deck again to fix one slide, instead of re-recording only that slide.

blocks.text: Where Lazur helps while you record

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. Hold Option + Command (⌥ ⌘) and ask about anything on your screen. If you cannot find the Record button, ask where it is. Lazur draws a circle and a label around it, so you know where to click.

If you want a walkthrough, ask Lazur to guide you. It waits for each click, so you stay in control of PowerPoint. Lazur does not record the slide show for you. It does not click buttons or operate PowerPoint. It points, explains and answers out loud.
Next steps after your first recording

Play the export twice, once with headphones and once through the laptop speakers. Check that the voice is clear and the slides change at the right moment. Then share the file. If you build decks often, the [PowerPoint page](/apps/powerpoint) covers more workflow help.
Lazur has a Pro trial with no credit card. The trial starts when you first open the app. You can get the app from the [download page](/download).

faq.question: Can I record a slide show in PowerPoint for the web on Mac?
faq.answer: No. Microsoft says PowerPoint for the web does not support recording slide shows. Use the desktop app, which Microsoft lists as supporting recording on Mac.

faq.question: Where is the Record Slide Show button in PowerPoint on Mac?
faq.answer: It depends on your build. Some builds show Slide Show > Record Slide Show. Others show a Record button in the top-right corner and a Record tab. Check the menu bar first, then the top-right corner.

faq.question: Is the narration saved in the presentation file?
faq.answer: Yes. Recordings are embedded in the slides and play during Slide Show. A separate video file is created only when you export the presentation as a video.

faq.question: What PowerPoint version do I need for narrated video?
faq.answer: Microsoft says narration is included in video exports from build 16.19. A Microsoft Q&A moderator named 16.60 for narrated recording, and another reply named 16.61. Use Help > Check for Updates if you are behind.

faq.question: Can I record only audio, without the camera?
faq.answer: Yes. Turn off the video button on the recording toolbar and PowerPoint records audio only. The audio still syncs with each slide.

faq.question: Do the Windows recording keys work on a Mac?
faq.answer: No. The R, S and Alt+S keys belong to the Windows recording dialog. On a Mac, use Esc to exit recording and Command+. to end the slide show.

faq.question: Can Lazur record the slide show for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate apps for you. It points at the Record button, explains options out loud, and guides you one click at a time while you do the recording.

steps.name: Check your PowerPoint build
steps.text: Open PowerPoint > About PowerPoint and read the version number. Video export with narration needs build 16.19 or newer. A Microsoft Q&A moderator named 16.60 for narrated recording, so update if you are below that.
steps.tip: Choose Help > Check for Updates if you need a newer build.

steps.name: Allow the microphone
steps.text: Open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone. Make sure PowerPoint is switched on. Then open System Settings > Sound > Input and confirm the microphone you want is selected.
steps.tip: Quit and reopen PowerPoint after you change this setting.

steps.name: Open the Record command
steps.text: Choose Slide Show > Record Slide Show. On builds with a Record button, click it in the top-right corner instead. Use Record > From Beginning or Record > From Current Slide if your Record tab offers them.
steps.tip: Start from the current slide when you only need to redo part of the deck.

steps.name: Choose Presenter view or Teleprompter
steps.text: Pick Presenter view to see your notes and the next slide while you talk. Pick Teleprompter if you read from a script. Either one works for a narrated recording.

steps.name: Set the audio and video devices
steps.text: Use the audio dropdown on the recording toolbar to choose your microphone. Use the video dropdown to choose your camera. Turn off the video button to record audio only.
steps.tip: Blur background is available in the camera options if your room is busy.

steps.name: Press Record and pause for a second
steps.text: Press Record. Wait a moment before you speak so the first slide starts clean. Use the pause button for breaks, then resume from the same spot.

steps.name: Move through slides and let transitions finish
steps.text: Advance with the arrow keys or a click. Narration does not record during a slide transition, so let the animation finish before you talk.

steps.name: Exit the recording
steps.text: Press Esc to exit the recording. Command+. also ends the slide show. Your narration and timings stay in the slides.

steps.name: Preview and re-record a slide
steps.text: Use Preview Play to watch the recording. To redo one slide, select the trash-can button to the left of Record, then record that slide again.
steps.tip: Clear Recording and Reset to Cameo are on the Record tab, for the current slide or all slides.

steps.name: Export to MP4 video
steps.text: Choose File > Export. In the File Format menu, pick MP4 with HEVC. Choose Ultra HD 4K, Full HD 1080p, HD 720p or Standard 480p, keep Use Recorded Timings and Narrations checked, then click Export.
steps.tip: Some builds also offer Record > Export to video.

troubleshooting.problem: The Record option is missing or greyed out
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm you are in the desktop app, since PowerPoint for the web cannot record. Update with Help > Check for Updates and look again. Microsoft's 2024 Tech Community post described a gradual rollout starting at build 16.43.

troubleshooting.problem: The microphone does not pick up your voice
troubleshooting.fix: Turn PowerPoint's microphone access off and on in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone, then quit and reopen the app. Check System Settings > Sound > Input. One Microsoft Q&A reply suggested this, but the asker said reinstalling did not help and no fix was confirmed.

troubleshooting.problem: Narration is missing from the MP4 export
troubleshooting.fix: Keep Use Recorded Timings and Narrations checked in the export window. Confirm your build supports narration in video, which Microsoft lists from 16.19. Play the file before you share it, because other embedded media may not export.

troubleshooting.problem: A slide's narration is cut off or clipped
troubleshooting.fix: Your speech probably started during a transition. Select the trash-can button left of Record, then record that slide again. Wait for the animation to finish before you speak.
